title: feat(hygon): support low-level FlashAttention dropout for FP16 and FP32
head: feat/hygon-fa-dropout-pr-20261112
body:
### PR Category

Operator / OP Test

### Type of Change

New Feature / Bug Fix

### Description

Enable non-zero dropout in the Hygon FlagGems low-level FlashAttention forward/backward pair for FP16 and FP32.

- Use pre-dropout softmax probabilities for normalization and LSE; apply the mask and inverse keep probability only to the value path and matching probability gradients.
- Reserve disjoint Philox ranges and return initialized seed/offset tensors so backward replays the forward mask.
- Correct dense backward dropout math, retain FP16 dot products with FP32 accumulation, and use IEEE dot products for FP32 dense backward.
- Preserve the probability-conversion residual in Hygon FP16/BF16 dense dV using an additional low-precision dot. Include dropout and compensation mode in the relevant autotune keys.
- Add independent CPU FP64 output/LSE/gradient references with replayed dropout masks. For the legacy Hygon zero-dropout test, derive dV from CPU FP64 math and retain the existing absolute/relative tolerances; native low-precision dV is not an exact oracle.
- When Hygon lacks a native cuDNN/memory-efficient reference, mark that reference-dependent case inapplicable only for the exact missing-operator or disabled-build errors. Numerical errors, unrelated failures, and other vendors retain their existing behavior. Six CPU controls check this boundary.

The tested feature contract is contiguous dense fixed-length BSHD square MHA, head dimensions 64/128, causal or non-causal, through `flag_gems._flash_attention_forward` and `flag_gems.flash_attention_backward`. Varlen backward is unchanged. Public Hygon SDPA dropout, `_scaled_dot_product_flash_attention` dropout integration, and mixed boxing-forward/FlagGems-backward routing remain follow-up work; these direct-backend tests do not claim their validation.

### Issue

Related to #8748 and flagos-ai/Torch-FL#795. The mixed-backend failure and public SDPA entry restrictions remain open.

### Progress

- [ ] Change is properly reviewed (1 reviewer required, 2 recommended).
- [x] Change is responded to an issue.
- [x] Change is fully covered by a UT.

### Performance

Correctness validation on Hygon BW, 2026-11-12:

| Suite | Cases | Coverage |
|---|---:|---|
| FP16 dropout | 28 passed | dropout 0/0.1/0.2/0.5; causal/non-causal; head dimensions 64/128; selected batches 1/2, sequence lengths 32/64/128, heads 2/4 |
| FP32 regression | 8 passed | dropout 0/0.2; causal/non-causal; head dimensions 64/128 |

These suites check output, LSE, dQ/dK/dV, shape/stride, finite values, Philox mask replay and non-overlapping reservations against independent CPU FP64 math. Production source is byte-identical to the hardware-tested `adbbf8010` tree; source hashes were checked after accounting for archive newline conversion. FP32 was repeated with an isolated compilation cache.

Official CI for head `69caccc0f` completed successfully on 2026-11-12: `rule-check-required`, NVIDIA `python-op`, Hygon `test-hygon`, and the final `unittest-required` all passed (unit-test run `43193569290`).

| Official CI selection | Hygon | NVIDIA |
|---|---|---|
| FP16 dropout suite | 28 passed | 28 skipped (Hygon-only) |
| FP32 regression suite | 8 passed | 8 skipped (Hygon-only) |
| Complete backward file | 76 passed / 756 skipped | 532 passed / 300 skipped |
| Forward-marker selection | 49 passed | 8 passed / 41 skipped |
| quick-cpu reference mode, FP16 / FP32 suites | 28 passed / 8 passed | Not claimed |

These are separate invocations with overlapping coverage; counts are not additive. Skipped cases are not counted as passing. The quick-cpu entries describe reference mode while the FlagGems kernels still run on the accelerator.

The Hygon backward-file skips comprise native-reference unavailability (192 cuDNN, 80 efficient, 480 scaled-efficient cases) and 4 pre-existing causal non-square exclusions. Its 76 passing cases include all 39 legacy low-level flash-backward cases, 28 valid existing flash-SDPA-backward adapter cases, 3 CPU dV controls and 6 availability controls. `pre-commit run --all-files` passed.

Local hardware environment: Hygon BW; DTK 26.04; Python 3.10.20; PyTorch `2.10.0+cpu`; Torch-FL `2.10.0+das.dtk2604.glibc228.g6d84d12b`; FlagTree `0.6.0+hcu3.6.glibc228.compat1.git8a1dda94` (Triton API 3.6.0); flash-attn `2.8.3+dtk2604.torch2100.2609141737.g103592`. The tested tensors/kernels run on DCU despite the PyTorch wheel suffix. Official Hygon CI separately used PyTorch `2.9.0+das.opt1.dtk2604` and flash-attn `2.8.3+das.opt1.dtk2604.torch290`, as recorded by its dependency reconciliation step. Additional vendor hardware validation is limited to the official NVIDIA CI described above.

Reproduce in a configured Torch-FL environment, loading its runtime before collecting tests:

```bash
python - <<'PY'
import torch_fl
import pytest
raise SystemExit(pytest.main([
    "-q", "--ref", "cpu",
    "tests/test_hygon_fp16_flash_attention_dropout.py",
    "tests/test_hygon_fp32_flash_attention_dropout.py",
    "tests/test_flash_attention_backward.py",
]))
PY
```

Informational comparison for the dV compensation: median synchronized backward Python API wall time in microseconds, 10 warmups and 50 alternating measurements per implementation, same inputs/device. Allocation, dispatch logging and synchronization are included; compilation/autotuning is warmed up. These are not isolated kernel timings or a speedup claim.

| B×S×H×D | dtype | dropout | Before compensation (us) | Current (us) | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1×64×2×64 | float16 | 0.0 | 342.4 | 342.6 | +0.06% |
| 1×64×2×64 | float16 | 0.2 | 416.4 | 408.6 | -1.86% |
| 2×512×4×64 | float16 | 0.0 | 398.7 | 403.5 | +1.22% |
| 2×512×4×64 | float16 | 0.2 | 483.7 | 493.2 | +1.97% |
| 1×64×2×64 | float32 | 0.2 | 396.6 | 397.0 | +0.11% |
